card.name: Hedging verbs after a possible cause
card.fires_on: The word right after a noun or 'may' in a cautious clinical statement, such as 'only', 'cannot', 'indicates' or 'represent'. It marks a hedged claim about a possible link or exclusion.

modes.label: Qualifier after symptom
modes.description: 'only' follows a condition name, limiting when the symptoms point to it.
modes.example: These symptoms may suggest OIH<< only>> if there is no evidence of underlying disease

modes.label: Older patients caveat
modes.description: 'cannot' follows 'greater sensitivity of some older individuals', in a statement that it cannot be ruled out.
modes.example: greater sensitivity of some older individuals<< cannot>> be ruled out.

modes.label: Verb linking finding to meaning
modes.description: A verb such as 'represent' or 'indicates' links a finding to what it might mean.
modes.example: there is concern that such symptoms may<< represent>> precursors to emerging suicidality.

card.writes: It seems to suppress hedge words like 'maybe' and 'possibly', since the hedge has already been given.
card.plain: It fires on the word that carries a cautious 'might be' or 'cannot be excluded' meaning in a label.
